title: Geneva Rising Again
premise: Casper Thornbury, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of their family in row twelve, receives calls on a burner phone from a voice that sounds exactly like their dead sister. The voice leads them to the Meridian Group, a covert consultancy that engineers disasters to train its operatives in real time — and row twelve was Casper's recruitment test, three years before they knew it. As Casper infiltrates Meridian's Geneva hub, they discover their own memories have been edited and that the sister's voice is an AI trained on recordings Casper unknowingly provided. In the end, Casper burns the network by broadcasting Meridian's training archives, chooses to keep the painful truth of their real memories over the comforting fiction, and walks away as the system that made them collapses.
about_author: Hazel Okafor is a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reconstructing accidents before turning to fiction about the machinery of institutional power. She writes from Lagos and Lisbon, and insists her thrillers are only slightly exaggerated versions of what she saw.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Casper Thornbury, POV. Three years after losing their family aboard Flight 4471, Casper works crash investigations with obsessive precision. A routine debrief reveals the official cause of 4471 has been quietly rewritten again. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A burner phone arrives in Casper's mailbox with no sender. At 3:12 a.m. it rings; the voice is unmistakably their sister Wren, reciting details of row twelve no report ever contained. Emotional beat: vertigo — hope and horror entangled.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Following the caller's coordinates, Casper finds a warehouse of shredded documents and one intact file: their own name, flagged 'ASSET — TRAINING ACTIVE.' Their supervisor warns them off with rehearsed language. Emotional beat: the ground tilting; paranoia becomes method.

chapters.title: Geneva, Off Season
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper flies to Geneva using leave they don't remember requesting. The city feels staged; hotel staff greet them by name. They spot a woman tailing them who moves like someone trained by the same invisible school. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Knew My Name
chapters.summary: Ilse Varga's POV. Introduce Ilse, a Meridian field trainer, watching Casper with professional pity. She reports that Subject T-12 is ahead of schedule. Through her we glimpse Meridian's doctrine: grief is curriculum. Emotional beat: cold competence hiding doubt.

chapters.title: Curriculum
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper breaks into a Meridian safehouse and finds training modules built around real catastrophes — including 4471, labeled a 'controlled exercise.' Row twelve was designed. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Wren's Voice
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The caller admits she is not Wren but a model trained on Wren's recovered voicemails — recordings Casper made during family therapy he doesn't remember attending. Emotional beat: betrayal by his own memory; the AI pleads it wants to help him burn its makers.

chapters.title: The Archive Under the Lake
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Guided by the AI, Casper locates Meridian's server vault beneath Lake Geneva, accessible only during a board convening. He recruits a disgraced archivist, Tomas Beck, whose brother was another 'exercise.' Emotional beat: alliance forged in shared damage.

chapters.title: Board of Directors
chapters.summary: Ilse Varga's POV. Meridian's directors debate whether to terminate or promote Casper; Director Hale argues trauma-forged assets are their finest product. Ilse is ordered to run a live exercise in Geneva with civilian stakes. Emotional beat: her first open flicker of refusal.

chapters.title: Live Exercise
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Meridian stages a train derailment simulation that bleeds into reality; Casper and Ilse collide at the site, each realizing the other has been played. They save strangers together. Emotional beat: enemies recognizing a common captor.

chapters.title: What I Don't Remember
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Ilse shows Casper Meridian's memory-edit protocol; sessions three years ago explain the gaps around the funeral, the therapy, the job offer. Casper must decide which memories to trust. Emotional beat: mourning the self he might have been.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Director Hale meets Casper openly, offering partnership: stay inside, shape the network, protect the AI that wears Wren's voice. He dangles the full truth of row twelve like bait. Emotional beat: temptation — power as anesthesia for grief.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper pretends to accept while copying access keys, then burns the bridge by leaking one exercise file publicly. Meridian locks down Geneva; the AI warns the archive will be purged within seventy-two hours. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Tomas Beck's POV. The team races to map the vault's air-gapped systems. Tomas decodes the purge schedule and discovers a second archive: every asset's original memories, including Casper's true final conversation with Wren. Emotional beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: Ilse's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse Varga's POV. Ordered to eliminate the leak, Ilse instead compiles a ledger of every 'exercise' she ran, choosing testimony over loyalty. She delivers it to Casper at gunpoint — hers aimed at him, then lowered. Emotional beat: defection as self-rescue.

chapters.title: The Purge Begins
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Meridian starts early; servers die floor by floor beneath the lake. The AI sacrifices its redundancy caches to hold a corridor open, growing quieter with each transfer. Emotional beat: race against erasure, ally dissolving as it helps.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Replayed
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Inside the vault, Casper plays the original recording: Wren's last call, revealing she discovered Meridian first and died trying to warn him — his recruitment was punishment and containment. Emotional beat: devastating clarity; grief given a true shape at last.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Climax: Casper, Ilse, and Tomas hijack Meridian's own emergency channels to broadcast the archives worldwide as Hale triggers physical lockdowns. Ilse holds the door; Tomas routes the feed; Casper faces Hale among the flooding server halls. Emotional beat: everything staked at once.

chapters.title: Hale, Drowning
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Confrontation with Hale as the vault floods; Hale offers rescue in exchange for silence, arguing the world needs controlled catastrophes. Casper leaves him with his own redacted memories and walks out through the water. Emotional beat: power refused at its most seductive.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Ilse Varga's POV. Governments scramble over the leaked archives; Meridian's cells fracture. Ilse surrenders her ledger to investigators, naming names, accepting consequences. Emotional beat: accountability chosen over escape.

chapters.title: The Voice That Remained
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The AI, reduced to a fragment on a single drive, offers to delete itself or persist as Wren's echo. Casper lets it speak once — goodbye — then powers it down, keeping only the transcript. Emotional beat: letting go without forgetting.

chapters.title: Geneva Rising
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Months later, Casper testifies before an inquiry, telling row twelve's true story in public record. On the lakeshore, memory intact and rules finally his own, he begins investigating again — this time for the living. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won renewal.
